Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.397/2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Thalassery,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 12/06/2020.
The sole respondent herein is the third respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 11/07/2015, while he was pillion riding on a motorcycle from Thumkur to Bangalore, bolero luggage vehicle bearing registration No.KA-04-MB/8149 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down, as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent/driver and the second respondent/owner remained ex parte.

sentences.text: The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy but denying negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending vehicle.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 was examined and Exts.A1 to A32 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral or documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.
Ext.X1 disability certificate was also marked .

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the first respondent/driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 85,57,000/- together with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional income

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the notional income of the claim petitioner fixed at 12,000/- is quite low as he was a final year engineering student and that his income ought to have been fixed at least at 20,000/- per month.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount that has been fixed by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and so no further enhancement is called for.
9.1.
Ext.A30 shows that the claim petitioner was a student of diploma in Mechanical Engineering.
This Court in M.A.C.A. Nos.305, 346, 380 & 2303 of 2020 dated 15/07/2025 has fixed the monthly income of final year engineering students as 20,000/-.
In the present case the claim petitioner being a student of diploma in Mechanical Engineering, I find that the income can be fixed at 15,000/- per month.
2025:KER:73070 Extra Nourishment 10.
It is submitted that an amount of 50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal under this head is quite low and hence the same needs to be appropriately enhanced.
Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel third respondent/insurer that reasonable amounts have been granted and hence no further amount need be granted.
10.1. Admittedly, in this case the disability of the claim petitioner has been found to be 100% .

In such circumstances, the extra nourishment of 60,000/- as claimed in the petition seems to be just Siddarth Menon vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55652179/
3 and reasonable.

sentences.text: Hence, extra nourishment of 60,000/- is awarded.
Bystander expenses 11.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that an amount of 17,28,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal under this head is quite low and hence the same needs to be appropriately enhanced.
On the other hand, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the amount that has been awarded is quite reasonable and no further enhancement is called for.

11.1. The Tribunal relying on the dictum in Kajal v.
2025:KER:73070 Jagdish Chand, (2020) 4 SCC 413 has adopted the multiplier method in awarding compensation.
The Tribunal has taken the attendant charges at the rate of 8,000/- per month.

However, going by the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Co. Ltd,
(2011) 13 SCC 236, the charges can be fixed at 10,000/- per month.

However, on going through the impugned Award, I find that reasonable amounts have been granted under the other heads and therefore, no further enhancement is called for.

In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 14,14,000/- (total compensation =99,71,000/- that is, 85,57,000/-
granted by the Tribunal + 14,14,000/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum 2025:KER:73070 from the date of petition till the date of realization and proportionate costs.
The third respondent/insurer is directed to deposit the compensation with interest and costs before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the compensation amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
